data.long_meaning: The name Clemente is derived from the Greek word 'klementos', meaning 'merciful' or 'mild'. In the Bible, Saint Clement is mentioned as one of the seven deacons appointed by the apostles to help the poor and needy in the early Christian community. He is also known as the first pope, having been elected to the position around AD 80.

He wrote several letters, most notably to the Corinthians, which were influential in shaping early Christian thought.

Clemente VII, born on January 25, 1478, was the Pope from 1523 to 1534.
